comments.body:
## Where the restart time goes (measured 2026-11-01, read-only)

**Crash window, 2026-10-29 UTC (nginx logs on the box):** OOM kill 00:47:26.7. 00:47:27 the 10 in-flight `/mcp` requests end (`upstream prematurely closed`); one `connect() failed (111)`; then 00:47:28 / :30 / :35 / :43 / :45 / :53 all `recv() failed (104: Connection reset by peer)`, meaning the published port accepted but nothing listened inside the container. The next `/mcp*` request, 00:48:14, was answered by the app (404 on `/mcp/health`). The container's own log for that restart is gone (it logged to json-file then; journald since creatable-isleted-kusimanse).

**Start-to-listen on the box, deploy of 2026-11-01 (container `rebar-mcp-e5a7e75b7fa7-8093`, journald):**

| UTC | step |
|---|---|
| 08:57:12.54 | container started (`State.StartedAt`) |
| 08:57:12.62 | entrypoint first line (provisioning forks to background) |
| 08:57:15.28 to 08:57:35.07 | `PARENT_CHAIN_FORK_RESOLVED` warnings from the reducer, i.e. the in-process boot ensure sweep (`run_startup_store_sweep`) replaying tickets |
| 08:57:36.93 | uvicorn `Started server process` |
| 08:57:36.97 | startup handshake done, `Uvicorn running` (handshake 0.04 s) |
| 08:57:38.66 | first `/health` 200 (autodeploy probe) |
| 08:57:38.87 | nginx cutover |

So 24.4 s pass before the process listens, and the listener is serving 0.04 s after that. nginx health gating adds nothing on a crash restart: nginx stays pointed at the same port.

**Phase timing, local, isolated copy of the tickets store (9,853 ticket dirs), `main()` steps timed individually, 2 runs:** import 0.29 / 0.17 s; boot ensure sweep 16.92 / 15.68 s; config 0.53 / 0.39 s; `build_server` 0.84 / 0.65 s. Inside the sweep, `snapshot-close-metadata` took 16.22 / 14.81 s; every other unit took 0.24 s or less.

**Comparison:** dewy-rotatable-tarsier measured container start to uvicorn start at 5.20 / 7.54 / 5.49 s on 2026-08-28. The `snapshot-close-metadata` unit landed in 3835269d792 (2026-10-28 11:18 PDT), which is an ancestor of f8ddcaf88e6, the build running at the 10-29 crash. docs/migrations.md already records "a converged sweep still costs about 21.5 s under the lock" and lists MCP boot as a run site. The sweep runs synchronously in `main()` before `build_server`/`run_mcp`, so that cost lands directly in time-to-listen.

On the box the entrypoint also runs the full ensure registry in the background (`reviewbot-ensure-tickets.sh`; it finished at 08:57:40.68, after bind), so the in-process boot sweep duplicates the registry run.

## Claude Code reconnect limits

- code.claude.com/docs/en/mcp: for a remote server that drops mid-session, Claude Code makes 5 attempts with exponential backoff starting at 1 s and doubling. In an interactive session it then marks the server failed and shows "open /mcp to reconnect". `/mcp reconnect all` needs v2.1.284 or later. In `claude -p` and Agent SDK sessions, after a transient error such as a 5xx, it keeps retrying in the background for up to about 30 minutes.
- The documented env vars (code.claude.com/docs/en/env-vars: `MCP_TIMEOUT`, `MCP_CONNECT_TIMEOUT_MS`, `MCP_TOOL_TIMEOUT`, `CLAUDE_CODE_MCP_*`) include none that changes the reconnect count or backoff.
- anthropics/claude-code#55228, "hardcoded 5-attempt reconnect cap", was closed as not planned (stale) on 2026-06-01. #101280, "HTTP MCP client gives up after ~15 s of connection-refused", has been open since 2026-10-11. A comment there reports that 2.1.299 headless added up to 8 background attempts after the ladder, while a desktop-hosted 2.1.299 session still gave up. The 10-29 session (2.1.308, interactive) logged "Max reconnection attempts (5) reached, giving up" with no background retry.

comments.body: Acceptance criteria rewritten 2026-11-01 on operator direction (option (20) chosen): the original ACs required an induced crash on the box, which is not permitted. The replacements prove locally that the server accepts MCP requests before the boot sweep finishes and that shutdown waits for it, and measure container start to server start on the first autodeploy after merge (read-only). Design: boot ensure sweep moves to a background thread holding the 1c51c9dcd06 drain gauge; lock arguments unchanged.

Regression test tests/unit/test_mcp_startup_sweep_background.py (6 tests) fails on the pre-fix main() ordering and passes on the fix. Targeted MCP, store-ensure and tombstone-guard tests: 403 passed, 13 skipped. make lint and make typecheck pass.

Patch set 2 (a41975c8a6fbaa5330377c2dd8d396888bd3c6f1) spawns it through spawn_context_daemon under tracked_work(gauge.hold), and adds a test for a RemovedInputError raised inside the background sweep (an LLM-Review advisory finding): it is logged at ERROR and the gauge is released. compiled_state.description:
## Observation

On 2026-10-28 at 17:47:26 PDT (2026-10-29 00:47:26 UTC) the kernel OOM-killed the on-box `rebar-mcp` process (bug teenage-unquieted-ringworm). Docker restarted it in place (`restart=always`, same port). nginx answered `/mcp` with 502 from 00:47:27 to at least 00:47:53 UTC. The resets show the port accepted connections but nothing listened inside the container. The app answered again by 00:48:14. Claude Code 2.1.308 made its 5 reconnect attempts (1 s backoff doubling), the last at 00:47:43, then gave up. The session stayed disconnected until a manual `/mcp` reconnect.

## Root cause (measured; evidence in comments)

`mcp_server.main()` runs `run_startup_store_sweep()` (the idempotent ensure registry, `rebar._store.ensures.run_ensures`) synchronously BEFORE `build_server`/`run_mcp`, so nothing listens until the sweep ends. Since 3835269d792 (2026-10-28) the registry includes `snapshot-close-metadata`, which costs about 15-22 s even on a converged store. Measured:

- On the box, 2026-11-01 deploy: container start 08:57:12.54 UTC → uvicorn `Started server process` 08:57:36.93 (24.4 s). The startup handshake took 0.04 s.
- Locally, on an isolated copy of the tickets store: sweep 15.7-16.9 s, of which `snapshot-close-metadata` was 14.8-16.2 s; import, config and `build_server` together were under 1.7 s.
- On 2026-08-28 (dewy-rotatable-tarsier) start → uvicorn was 5.2-7.5 s.

Claude Code has no setting to raise its reconnect count (code.claude.com/docs/en/mcp, /env-vars; anthropics/claude-code#55228 closed not-planned, #101280 open). The fix therefore has to be server-side.

## Prior intent

`run_startup_store_sweep`'s docstring says the sweep "skips contention rather than delaying service". trivial-protected-barracuda rejected a warm standby and blue/green self-heal (memory doubling) and chose an in-place restart, so restart speed is the lever.

## Plan

1. `src/rebar/_mcp_health.py`: add `start_startup_store_sweep(gauge)`.
   - It resolves the tracker path synchronously, so a `RemovedInputError` from config still aborts startup, and the missing-store warning stays synchronous.
   - It then runs the ensure sweep on a background daemon thread. Before the thread starts, it takes `gauge.hold()` (the same hold the 1c51c9dcd06 drain counts) and releases it in a `finally`. `run_mcp`'s `wait_for_idle` and the SIGTERM drain therefore wait for the sweep, and the signer key copy outlives it.
   - The sweep body keeps the same call, `run_ensures(tracker, timeout=5, attempts=1)`, so lock semantics are unchanged. The existing exception handling moves into the thread unchanged: debug-log anything else, error-log a `RemovedInputError` that reaches the thread, since a thread cannot abort the process.
   - `run_startup_store_sweep()` keeps its synchronous behaviour and signature for its existing callers and tests, and shares the sweep body.
2. `src/rebar/mcp_server.py` `main()`: build the server first, then call `start_startup_store_sweep` with the server's wired gauge, then `run_mcp`.
3. `docs/migrations.md`: state that the MCP-boot sweep runs in the background after the server starts, is waited for at shutdown, and has unchanged lock behaviour.
4. Regression test `tests/unit/test_mcp_startup_sweep_background.py`.

Out of scope: changing the ensure units or their cost, nginx/compose/autodeploy, and the client.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] AC1: With `run_ensures` patched to block on an event, `mcp_server.main()` reaches `run_mcp` while the sweep is still blocked. Proven by `pytest tests/unit/test_mcp_startup_sweep_background.py`, which fails on the pre-fix ordering.
- [ ] AC2: While the sweep is blocked, a server built by `build_server` with its health wiring answers an MCP `initialize` POST with 200 through its ASGI app. Same test file.
- [ ] AC3: The sweep thread holds the server's in-flight gauge (value 1 while blocked, 0 after release), and `rebar._mcp_serving.wait_for_idle` does not return until the sweep finishes. Same test file.
- [ ] AC4: The sweep thread calls `run_ensures` with `timeout=5, attempts=1` (lock semantics unchanged), and a `RemovedInputError` from tracker resolution still propagates synchronously from `start_startup_store_sweep`. Same test file; the existing `tests/unit/test_mcp_health_store_status.py` boot-sweep tests still pass.
- [ ] AC5 [non-codebase]: On the first MCP autodeploy after merge, the box journal shows container start (`docker inspect` `State.StartedAt`) → uvicorn `Started server process` under 10 s.
      provenance: environment=AWS account 896586841071 us-east-1, instance i-00880b2c7f13527c5 (rebar-gerrit); principal=frontier profile operator via read-only `aws ssm send-command` (AWS-RunShellScript, docker inspect + journalctl -t rebar-mcp); privilege_posture=production-equivalent; instrument=live-call — the measurement reads the production container's own start time and log, and no repository snapshot can replay that.
- [ ] AC6: `make lint` and `make typecheck` pass.

## File impact

- `src/rebar/_mcp_health.py`: background sweep starter.
- `src/rebar/mcp_server.py`: `main()` ordering.
- `docs/migrations.md`: MCP-boot sweep timing.
- `tests/unit/test_mcp_startup_sweep_background.py`: regression test.
